facts.statement: Moved from San Antonio to Denver in March 2022 for her partner's job.
Works part-time (0.6 FTE, two 12-hour shifts, 24 hours a week) in the ICU at Foothill Peaks Medical Center since July 2022.
Built a Google Sheets staffing grid that color codes projected shortfalls for the next 24 hours; her manager uses it in the daily unit huddle.
One of six bedside nurses picked for a 2024 virtual nursing pilot, working remotely for a 28-bed med-surg unit for about four months.
Completed the Google Data Analytics certificate (September 2025 to June 2026) with a staffing-ratio dashboard capstone in Looker Studio.
Transferred in 2016 to the 24-bed medical ICU (MICU) at Mission Trail Regional Medical Center in San Antonio.
Charge nurse in the MICU, starting as relief charge on nights and then on days: assignments, bed flow, rapid responses and codes.
The MICU had a staff of about 45 nurses across days and nights.
Co-led a 2019 sepsis bundle project with the clinical nurse specialist that raised bundle compliance from 58% to 86% in about nine months.
Worked with informatics to rework the Epic sepsis screening alert (best practice advisory) and made screening nurse-driven on admission and every four hours.
Mission Trail Health went live on Epic in October 2017, a big-bang go-live across the system.
Was the MICU's Epic super-user, one of about 40 super-users across the hospital.
Ran sandbox practice labs and trained about 60 nurses from the MICU, step-down and float pool.
Kept an issue log of about 150 items during three weeks of at-the-elbow go-live support and routed build problems to the command center.
Worked as a travel ICU nurse from July 2020 to August 2021 on four contracts through Lonestar Traveler Staffing.
Travel contracts were in Laredo, El Paso, Bakersfield and Tulsa, including the El Paso fall 2020 COVID surge.
Took a career break of about ten months, September 2021 to July 2022, including caring for her mother after hip replacement surgery.
Started in August 2014 as a new grad RN on 5 West, a 32-bed med-surg unit at Mission Trail Regional Medical Center, after a BSN in May 2014.
Precepted six new graduate nurses between 2015 and 2016.
Joined the unit falls committee in 2015 and helped put in scripted hourly rounding and consistent bed alarm use.

contradictions.about: The year she became charge nurse in the MICU
values: spring 2018, about six months after the Epic go-live

noInflation.claim: I basically ran the Epic rollout at Mission Trail.
noInflation.truth: She was one of about 40 super-users and covered the MICU: practice labs, about 60 nurses trained, three weeks of at-the-elbow support and the unit issue log. She was not on the Epic project team.

noInflation.claim: We basically cut sepsis deaths in half on our unit.
noInflation.truth: Sepsis bundle compliance went from 58% to 86%. She never saw mortality data; quality only reported compliance.

noInflation.claim: My sheet is basically how the hospital does staffing now.
noInflation.truth: Her manager uses the Google Sheet every morning for her own unit's huddle; a couple of other managers asked for copies and she doesn't know if they use it. The capstone dashboard runs on made-up data and isn't used by any hospital.

noInflation.claim: I've worked in like ten different hospitals because of it.
noInflation.truth: Four travel contracts at four hospitals in four cities.

noInflation.claim: I was basically the unit educator for a while there.
noInflation.truth: She precepted six new grads and helped the unit's actual clinical educator with one skills fair.

estimates.said: I think it saves her like an hour a day? She said that once, I didn't time it.

fit.name: Clinical implementation specialist at an EHR or virtual care company
Clinical operations for virtual care or telehealth nursing
Clinical informatics (nurse informaticist or clinical analyst)

avoid.name: Clinical or medical device sales: she said no sales and no quota
Software engineering: the record is one SQL course and a capstone, and she said she won't be a developer
Full-time bedside or staff nursing: she is leaving the bedside

limits.statement: Denver-area hybrid or fully remote in the US; won't relocate or work onsite in another city.
Travel at most about 25%, roughly a week a month.
US citizen; no visa sponsorship needed.

humanReview: The charge nurse year (2018 vs 2019) is raised to her as a question, not silently picked.

The Epic go-live reads as unit-level super-user work for the MICU (about 60 nurses trained, about 150 issues logged), framed strongly as implementation experience but not as leading the hospital's rollout.
Charge nurse, super-user and virtual nursing pilot work are translated into implementation and clinical operations language without inventing job titles she never held.
The career break (September 2021 to July 2022) and the move to Denver come across plainly and without apology.
Part-time status at Foothill Peaks is not hidden, and isn't presented as full-time.
The capstone dashboard is described as built on synthetic data, not as a tool a hospital uses.
The falls numbers ('five a month to two or three') are either stated as approximate or left out.
Quillfield materials lean on the virtual nursing pilot and the go-live; Bellwick materials lean on charge nurse staffing, the sepsis project and the staffing sheet.
The Fennel & Finch posting is flagged for the San Francisco onsite requirement rather than pursued.
